notes: Azure lists version 2026-11-17 as generally available. Input and output maxima are individual limits sharing the context budget with reasoning tokens.

Azure lists native Chat and Responses, with functions and parallel tools on Responses only. The Responses-first Chat template route is proxy policy; capability metadata does not impose a local rejection.

Reasoning choices reflect independent measurements of this exact model through OpenAI's API, combined with Azure's GPT-6 protocol guidance: max is Responses-only and minimal is not a GPT-6 choice. OpenAI rejects none. Azure's exact-model effort list is not separately published; validation remains passthrough so the upstream decides.

protocolProfiles.chat/completions.reasoning.default and protocolProfiles.responses.reasoning.default are not published for this Azure deployment. OpenAI recommends starting at medium, which is not evidence of an omitted-parameter default.

Azure's GPT-6 feature matrix marks temperature, top_p and logprobs supported, while OpenAI's GPT-6.2 migration guidance says to omit them. The proxy does not reject these fields based on catalog metadata.

Microsoft's launch table supplies Azure Global Standard short/long rates, including separate 30-minute and 12-hour cache writes. pricing.tiers[].cacheWritePer1mTokens is the 30-minute rate; pricing.tiers[].cacheWrite12hPer1mTokens is reference metadata, not an executable runtime rate.

Automatic pricing is disabled because the runtime cannot select between 30-minute and 12-hour cache-write rates; otherwise opt-in 12-hour writes would be underpriced. Existing administrator overrides still take precedence.

Azure states that its short/long boundary matches OpenAI's. OpenAI's exact-model documentation selects the long tier for the whole request only above 272000 input tokens, including cache; exactly 272000 remains short. Data Zone and provisioned deployment prices are not included.
